correctness.rationale: Two nonzero Laplacian spectral projections give exact uniform nonedge and edge kernels. The ratio (1-e^{-b^alpha t})/(1-e^{-a^alpha t}) strictly decreases from (b/a)^alpha to 1; hence the positive-time threshold exists uniquely iff alpha>1. All edge and diagonal entries remain positive. Counting row sums yield the exact ℓ^∞/ℓ^1 norms and a unique transient peak. With h(z)=-log(qe^{-z}-q+1), h′>0 and log(h′) strictly convex, which proves monotonic increase of z h′/h and therefore the unique global maximizing exponent, without relying on sampling. Fixed-graph expansions and limit equations prove the claimed rates. The attached checker passed 568 independent matrix-time comparisons, 32 scale checks and 800 global optimization samples; finite samples are not used to infer global uniqueness.

originality.rationale: The decisive novel component is the proof that the sharp positivity-recovery delay as a function of fractional power alpha>1 has one and only one global optimizer on every connected noncomplete strongly regular graph, including primitive examples, with an explicit scalar characterization. Direct full-document comparisons found the published complete-multipartite fractional graph result covers imprimitive equal-part subfamilies but does not assert unique-order optimization. Earlier qualitative semigroup criteria and the fractional random walk studies do not imply this optimizer. Other graph-heat source families use different rational or polynomial filters. Thus the narrow complete-multipartite positivity/peak formulas are acknowledged as covered, not claimed as newly discovered. Residual unindexed-priority risks remain.
residual_risks: The complete-multipartite fractional-heat prior covers part of the displayed non-optimizer statements; only the non-implied global exponent optimizer and extension to primitive strongly regular graphs are offered as novel.
A wider unindexed spectral-filter or graph semigroup optimization theorem could imply this result despite no such source appearing in the actual searches.
The initial 2015 version of the eventual-positivity source was not separately checked against its later full-text revision; only the revised full text was read.
No independent external expert mathematical audit has occurred.

value.rationale: The graph family is a natural complete spectral class containing primitive Petersen, pentagonal, triangular, and rook examples. The distinctive invariant is the globally unique fractional exponent at which positivity is delayed the most, not a routine special-case arithmetic result. The theorem also shows a nonzero limiting maximum operator-norm amplification even as the recovery window collapses at large fractional order. These facts quantitatively refine qualitative eventual positivity and inform stability of high-order graph diffusion.
